title: Record card debt, sarcastic cut - Maya's $100/month plan
caption: Maya's very adult plan: $100 a month on a $5K card. The bank loved it. Here's the math.

lines.text: Congratulations, America. We just set a new record.
One point two nine trillion dollars. In credit card debt.

visual.label: US credit card debt. a new record.

lines.text: That's straight from the New York Fed. Just in time for holiday shopping.

visual.idea: everything is fine while on fire
visual.label: the American wallet heading into the holidays

lines.text: So let's meet Maya. Twenty four. Financially responsible. Allegedly.
Maya has five thousand dollars on a card charging about twenty one percent.
Which, fun fact, is basically the average rate right now. So, not unlucky. Just normal.
Maya's plan? Pay a hundred bucks a month. Very adult.
She feels incredible about it.

visual.label: maya after setting up $100 autopay on a 21% card

lines.text: Here's the fun part. Eighty seven fifty of that first payment? Just interest.
So her actual balance drops by twelve dollars and fifty cents.
Twelve fifty.

visual.label: maya seeing her $5,000 balance go down by $12.50

lines.text: At this pace, she's paying that card for ten whole years.
Her card will be paid off around the same time she finally gets a raise.

visual.label: maya waiting for her card to be paid off

lines.text: And the interest? Almost seven thousand dollars. On a five thousand dollar balance.
So she paid for her stuff. And then paid for it again. Plus tip.

visual.text: so i bought it once... and then paid for it again??

lines.text: Now, plot twist. Same card. Same balance. Two fifty a month instead.
She's done in twenty five months.
Interest? About twelve hundred bucks. Not seven thousand.
That's fifty eight hundred dollars that stays with Maya, instead of the bank.

visual.label: maya paying $250 a month vs maya paying $100 a month

lines.text: So how do people actually get out? Paying more than the minimum. Hitting the highest rate card first. Or just calling and asking for a lower rate.
Yes. You can just ask. Wild, I know.

visual.label: finding out you can just ASK for a lower rate

lines.text: Because five thousand dollars of stuff should not cost twelve.
So what's the APR on your card? Be honest. Comments.

claims.claim: US credit card balances hit a record ~$1.29 trillion ($1.285T) in Q3 2026
Average credit card rate about 21% (Fed G.19: 21.19% all accounts, 22.36% accounts assessed interest)

$5,000 at 21% APR: first month's interest $87.50, so principal drops $12.50; $100/mo takes 120 months and $6,986 interest (total ~$11,986); $250/mo takes 25 months and $1,208 interest; difference $5,778

research_sources.title: New York Fed - Household Debt and Credit Report, Q3 2026 (Nov 10, 2026)
Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit release (Nov 6, 2026)
Bankrate - current credit card interest rates (avg 19.71%, Nov 4, 2026)
